title: Opportunity-cost mixmodel: prewarm vs fallback — notes
body:
Purpose:
This note is a working scratchpad to capture a compact, spreadsheet-style mix-model for tradeoffs between proactive prewarming and reactive fallback (spot/on-demand mixes) across regions. Goal: produce an actionable threshold and a minimal implementation checklist for the routing policy team (canary by customer tier).

High-level assumptions (baseline):
- Service SLO: p95 <= 220ms for interactive chat traffic, target cost-per-1k-tokens = $0.55 (hosted mold).
- Prewarm cost: keeping N GPUs hot costs $X/hr per GPU (example: g16x -> $2.40/hr fully loaded in dedicated pool).
- On-demand cold start penalty: average additional latency 300–1200ms depending on model and sequence length; tail worse on evictions.
- Spot eviction rate: region A historically 3% per hour, region B 9% per hour in 2am-6am window.
- Traffic mix: 70% interactive short prompts (avg 32 tokens), 30% long completions (avg 256 tokens).
- Model variants: base (big, higher cost), trimmed (quantized 4-bit, 20–30% cheaper, slightly lower quality).

Micro-spreadsheet: (rows mimic columns in a sheet)
Columns: Scenario | Prewarm GPUs | Prewarm cost/hr | Expected avoided fallback % | Avg tokens/hr | Fallback mix (spot:on-demand) | Est. fallback cost/hr | Net cost delta/hr | Notes
A1 Conservative prewarm | 8 | $19.20 | 80% | 120k | 70:30 | $7.80 | -$11.40 (save vs full fallback)
A2 Minimal prewarm | 2 | $4.80 | 30% | 120k | 50:50 | $10.90 | +$6.10 (worse)
B1 Aggressive prewarm + regional spread | 16 | $38.40 | 92% | 320k | 80:20 | $16.00 | -$22.40 (save)
C1 No prewarm (full fallback) | 0 | $0.00 | 0% | 200k | 60:40 | $29.50 | $29.50 (baseline)

Notes on numbers: fallback cost/hr is simplified estimate combining token cost (per-token spot/on-demand rates) + estimated cold-start compute waste (first token overhead). Net cost delta/hr computed relative to C1 baseline. This is intentionally coarse — exact cells will live in the spreadsheet.

Opportunity-cost framing: For moderate traffic patterns, prewarming small pools (2–8 GPUs) yields positive ROI if avoided fallback fraction > ~60% for the target SLO. The breakeven prewarm avoidance percentage is a function of token throughput and spot reliability (eviction rate).

Scenario sensitivity (quick mental model):
- If spot eviction probability doubles, fallback cost increases non-linearly due to retries and higher on-demand usage. The breakeven prewarm avoidance rises by ~12–18 percentage points.
- If average tokens per request rise (more long completions), per-request cost increases faster on on-demand; prewarm becomes more attractive.
- Regional imbalance: cheaper spot markets in region C reduce the need to prewarm there, but network egress / latencies might push routing to on-demand in closer regions.

Routing-policy recommendations (draft):
1) Tier-based prewarm windows: keep small warm pools (2–4 GPUs) for Free/Starter customers during local business hours; scale to 6–8 GPUs for PLG+ and enterprise teams with SLA.
2) Eviction-aware fallback weights: when spot eviction rate > 5% in last 30m, increase on-demand fraction by 20% for new requests to reduce client-visible retries.
3) Prewarm hysteresis: only spin-down prewarm pools if sustained low utilization for > 10 minutes to avoid oscillation costs.
4) Model-variant fallback ordering: prefer quantized-trimmed variants as first fallback (cheaper) if quality delta within customer-configured threshold; only escalate to on-demand full model when trimmed quality drop triggers eval alerts.

Implementation checklist (minimal MVP):
- [ ] Add telemetry counters: live spot eviction counts per region, prewarm utilization per GPU, cold-start tail latency histogram (p99, p995). Link: RD-2147.
- [ ] Routing policy config: 3 knobs (prewarm_count_by_tier, eviction_sensitivity_pct, coldstart_hysteresis_sec).
- [ ] Small simulation run: re-run routing-sim (PR#82) with 7 day history, vary spot eviction 0→15% to produce cost vs SLO curves.
- [ ] Canary rollout: 5% of enterprise customers for 48h with increased prewarm to verify p95 improvements and cost delta.

Open questions / data needs:
- Need historical per-region spot eviction heatmaps aligned to customer timezones (requesting SRE dataset export).
- How to quantify quality degradation tolerance per customer automatically? (suggestion: use recent eval score deltas mapped to feature flags).
- Need clearer @billing input: exact prewarm per-GPU cost used for forecasting (on dedicated vs hosted internal pricing).

Risk matrix (short):
- Over-prewarming -> increased fixed costs and wasted capacity during long low-traffic periods. Mitigation: autoscale aggressive down after hysteresis + watch utilization.
- Under-prewarming -> client-visible tail latency spikes, potential SLA breaches. Mitigation: faster fallback/auto-escalation routes, better trimmed-variant quality checks.
- Model-quality regressions from using trimmed variants as fallback. Mitigation: explicit quality acceptance thresholds per route and automated regression alerts (link to alerting playbook).

Next steps (this doc):
- Convert the micro-spreadsheet above into real sheet: columns with break-even formulas, region parameters, and time-windowed bidding curves (owner: Jon Kim, due: 2026-03-10).
- Run routing-sim sensitivity matrix for spot eviction 0, 3, 6, 12% (owner: Marina, due: 2026-03-15).
- Draft config PR for routing policy knobs and default values (owner: Ravi, target milestone 2026-Q2).

Quick reference cells (to copy into sheet):
- Prewarm cost per GPU/hr = $2.40 (example)
- On-demand token cost per 1k tokens = $0.80
- Spot token cost per 1k tokens = $0.28 (with eviction overhead multiplier 1.25x when eviction occurs)
- Cold-start overhead per new container = 0.25 CPU-hrs equivalent (accounted into first-10-token bucket)

Slack notes (raw):
- "If we can get eviction alerts down to <4% for region B we don't need to prewarm as much during EU nights" — @ellen_chu 2026-02-21
- "Trimmed variant has passed most evals for paragraph summarization but fails on rare NER cases" — @marina 2026-02-14

Bottom line (one-line):
Modest, tiered prewarm plus eviction-aware fallback mixing often reduces expected cost while preserving p95 SLOs — the math is sensitive to spot eviction rates and traffic composition, so fast-feedback telemetry and a small simulation matrix are required before wider rollout.

Document history: rough working doc; will be extracted into canonical spreadsheet and a proposal brief for PLG/Sales later.
